free_tier.stated: no free token allowance is advertised: serverless inference is prepaid, with credits bought after a payment method is added. Without a payment method or credits the account is held to 10 requests per minute account-wide; a $1 starter credit is mentioned in the credits FAQ, but whether a new account still receives one is unverified: behind a sign-up.
free_tier.notes: the pricing page of 2026-11-03 prints no signup credit; the credits FAQ still carries a '$1 starter credit' heading

interface_detail: OpenAI-compatible chat completions at https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1; an Anthropic-compatible endpoint at https://api.fireworks.ai/inference is also documented; documented, not…
tooling: the Fireworks Python SDK, the OpenAI SDK or the Anthropic SDK pointed at the Fireworks base URL, or curl; the firectl CLI shows quotas ('firectl quota list')
chaining: hosted lanes only: the same prepaid balance pays for serverless, on-demand deployments and training; the 6,000 RPM cap is one envelope shared by all of them

limits.value: 10 requests per minute account-wide while the account has no payment method or no credits; 6,000 requests per minute maximum with a payment method and active credits. The cap is fixed, shared by every model and every API, and requests above it are rejected (for example HTTP 429).

serverless token limits are per model and adaptive (total prompt, uncached prompt and generated tokens per minute); the published ceilings are the Tier 3 maximum, and tiers below Tier 3 have lower, unpublished ceilings
a monthly spend limit can be set; when usage reaches 100% of it all API requests pause until it is raised

binding_note: the account-wide request cap binds first: 10 RPM without a payment method or credits, 6,000 RPM with both; tokens are paid from prepaid credits, not granted free.

identity_cost.detail: an email address or a Google, GitHub or LinkedIn sign-in creates the account, but the 10 RPM state ends only after a valid payment method and billing address are added and credits are bought; an account that finishes its $1 starter credit with no payment method is suspended. Whether the sign-up asks for a phone number is unverified: behind a sign-up. Debit and prepaid card acceptance are not stated.

reliability_note: an account that finishes its $1 starter credit with no payment method is suspended until one is added; with credits exhausted and Auto Reload off, usage pauses until credits are added.
confidence_note: the 10 RPM and 6,000 RPM request limits, the prepaid-credits model and the payment-method requirement are quoted from vendor pages; the starter credit and the sign-up steps after the first are unverified: behind a sign-up.

evidence.quote: | No payment method or no credits | 10 RPM |
evidence.proved: an account with no payment method or no credits is held to 10 requests per minute, account-wide

evidence.quote: | Payment method and active credits | 6,000 RPM (maximum) |
evidence.proved: an account with a payment method and active credits is held to a 6,000 requests per minute maximum

evidence.quote: The 6,000 RPM cap applies account-wide—it is not a separate serverless-only limit—and it is a fixed ceiling, not adaptive.
evidence.proved: the 6,000 RPM ceiling is one fixed account-wide cap, not a serverless-only or adaptive limit

evidence.quote: Pay per token with pre-paid, usage-based billing. Simply add a payment method to buy credits, and usage is then deducted from your balance.
evidence.proved: serverless inference is prepaid: a payment method is added first, credits are bought, and usage is deducted from the balance

evidence.quote: Add a valid payment method and billing address, then purchase credits.
evidence.proved: credits are bought after a valid payment method and billing address are added

evidence.quote: Without payment method: Your account will be suspended until you add a payment method.
evidence.proved: an account that finishes its $1 starter credit with no payment method is suspended until one is added

evidence.quote: Sign up with Google Sign up with GitHub Sign up with LinkedIn
evidence.proved: the account-creation form offers an email address or a Google, GitHub or LinkedIn sign-in at its first step
the serverless endpoint is an OpenAI-compatible base URL

evidence.quote: The table shows the maximum ceilings, available at Tier 3 and above. Tiers below Tier 3 have lower ceilings.
evidence.proved: the published per-model serverless token ceilings are the Tier 3 maximum; lower tiers have lower unpublished ceilings

evidence.quote: When usage reaches 100% of the limit, all API requests pause automatically across serverless inference, deployments, and training.
evidence.proved: a monthly spend limit pauses all API requests when reached

notes: per-token prices (USD per 1M tokens) are published on the serverless pricing page; the 10 RPM lane is not a usable free tier, because no free credit is advertised and an account with no payment method that spends its starter credit is suspended.
